question:
Whose
house?

beats.text: John gave his cloak to every beggar he met.
Then he walked to Our Lady of Guadalupe, to pray.
beats.scene: A vast dry Spanish mountain landscape at dusk under a huge stormy sky: on a far ridge the dark fortress-like walls and towers of a great monastery with a hard light on its stone; far below on a winding stony road a single tiny pilgrim with a staff, seen from far behind, walks toward it. Skewed angular rocks, drifting mist. No faces.

beats.text: Back in Granada, he rented a house for the sick poor.
One account says he carried them in on his own shoulders.
By night, he begged for them, street by street.
beats.scene: A narrow sixteenth-century Granada street at night under a hard moon: one tiny figure in a cloak with a hood, seen from far behind, stands at a closed wooden door with a hand raised to knock, a small lantern at his feet throwing a pool of light on the cobbles; skewed angular houses on either side, mist at the ground. No faces.

beats.text: The Bishop of Tuy gave him a habit, for his own.
And it was the bishop who fixed his name: John of God.
beats.scene: A dim sixteenth-century bishop's study: a heavy carved wooden desk with an open parchment, a quill in an inkwell and a single candle, a tall high-backed chair empty behind it, a dark episcopal cloak and a plain coarse habit folded together on a corner of the desk; hard shaft of light from a high arched window, drifting dust. No people.

beats.text: Others began to join him, one by one.
